text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Centre Democrat leader, Mimi Jakobsen, is asking for the age for early retirement to be raised from the present 60 years to 62 years. The party, which pledged to continue supporting the government after quitting the coalition at Christmas, is now warning the dominant Social Democrats not to change the composition of the rump coalition with the Radical Liberals.

--- The Danish state is to make a complaint to the international court for human rights in Strasbourg today, accusing the Turkish state for having tortured an ethnic Kurdish Danish citizen after arresting him during a family visit to Turkey last summer.

--- Some 2600 people employed by the Danish state railways ferry division will lose their jobs when the Great Belt bridge and tunnel link between the island of Zealand and the Jutland peninsula becomes operational.

--- Local authorities want to lower housing benefits for the elderly, saying that 50 to 75 percent of pensioners getting housing benefits from the state are granted too much and should have their benefits lowered or taken away.

--- Denmark continues to lose large market shares abroad. Industrial exports should have risen by six percent last year if Denmark was to get its relative share of growth in major foreign markets, the Confederation of Danish Industries says.
--- The government is prepared to reduce rent subsidies by a total two billion crowns over the next 15 years, pensioners will bear the brunt of the change.
